structure.title: A marriage defended
structure.text: The opening establishes the couple's mutual commitment amid objections and a move from Venice to military Cyprus.

structure.title: Interpretation manipulated
structure.text: Iago arranges conversations and apparent evidence, allowing suspicion to acquire the force of discovery.

people.name: Othello
people.text: A Moorish general trusted by Venice to defend Cyprus, proud of his service and newly married, who is at ease on the battlefield and less so in Venetian society.

people.name: Desdemona
people.text: A Venetian senator's daughter who has married Othello secretly and defends her choice before the Senate, loving him for the stories of his life.

people.name: Iago
people.text: Othello's ensign, passed over for promotion, who is known to everyone as honest Iago and tells the audience early on that he is not what he seems.

context.title: An outsider's standing
context.text: Othello's military value coexists with racial hostility and social insecurity. Recognition in one role does not guarantee trust in another.
context.takeaway: Listen to how others describe his belonging.

context.title: Unequal knowledge
context.text: The audience hears Iago's planning while his targets hear his performance. Suspense comes from watching interpretation go wrong.
context.takeaway: Separate what is seen from what is inferred.

notice.why: Reluctance can make a speaker seem trustworthy.
Meaning depends on a story attached to possession.

opening: Othello and Desdemona have married against her father's wishes, trusting each other enough to withstand the scandal. Iago begins with suggestions so slight that they scarcely sound like accusations. He knows which questions to leave unfinished and when to appear reluctant to speak. Shakespeare makes the destruction of trust unfold through gestures that could mean anything and a listener increasingly desperate for certainty. The audience can see the deception working while the person inside it experiences each new suspicion as an advance towards the truth.
